answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing: instance directories are devices/<device>/<n> under the instance root (instance_path builds exactly that), and a numeric directory name IS an existing instance. Not assumed: that every number has a running process; this reads only what exists on disk. Akien (outline 5.3.5.2.2): 'we have a cc_0 instance, so I'll launch it with cc_1' presupposes something that can say which numbers are taken.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs: the file (cairn/tools/base/address.py), the exact signatures (instances(device, roots=None) -> list[int]; next_free_instance(device, roots=None) -> int), that roots follow the same default as instance_path (ROOTS), that nothing is created (reading must not mkdir), and a proof over a scratch roots dict. The ticket carries all of these.

answers.collision_check: Looked at address.py's instance_path/log_path/tool_path/machine_path (path builders; none lists) and ticket d13859e2ae46 (shim naming), which this is a dependency of at orchestrator's ruling (address owns instance directory reads, not shim.py). No collision: this adds two read-only functions and changes none.
answers.falsifier_check: Clauses: (1) instances(device, roots) returns the sorted integers named by the numeric directories under <instance root>/devices/<device>, ignoring non-numeric names, and [] when the device folder is absent | (2) next_free_instance(device, roots) returns the lowest non-negative integer not in that list, so [0, 2] gives 1 and [] gives 0. Horizon: red against HEAD (neither function exists), green after.
answers.gates_bound: proof gate (a hollow build must fail it) + durability gate (committed) + feeds-back-to-origin on failure (Laws 3 + 8).
answers.missing_check: Not wrapped: whether an instance whose directory exists but whose process is gone counts as taken. This ticket says yes (a directory is an instance's home and its state; reusing the number would reuse another instance's state), and names it; liveness is the shim's own presence and is out of this tool's reach.
